doc_name: Patiala and East Punjab States Union
text: The Patiala and East Punjab States Union (PEPSU) was a state of India formed by uniting eight princely states—seven Punjab states and one Punjab Hill State—between 1948 and 1956. The capital and principal city was Patiala, and the state covered an area of 26,208 km², including Kasauli, Kandaghat, and Chail. It was inaugurated on 15 July 1948 and formally became a state of India in 1950. On 1 November 1956, PEPSU was merged mostly into Punjab State under the States Reorganisation Act. Parts of PEPSU, including the present-day Jind district (Jind & Narwana), Pinjore in north Haryana, and Charkhi Dadri, Bawal, and Mahendragarh Narnaul in south-west Haryana, now lie within the state of Haryana, which was separated from Punjab on 1 November 1966. Other areas, such as Kandaghat, Solan, and Nalagarh, are now in Himachal Pradesh. The then-Maharaja of Patiala, Yadavindra Singh, was appointed Rajpramukh (equivalent to Governor) and served throughout the state's existence; the Maharaja of Kapurthala, Jagatjit Singh, served as Uparajpramukh (lieutenant-governor). Gian Singh Rarewala was sworn in as the first Chief Minister on 13 January 1949, followed by Col. Raghbir Singh on 23 May 1951, with Brish Bhan as Deputy Chief Minister. The state elected a 60-member legislative assembly on 6 January 1952, with the Congress Party winning 26 seats and the Akali Dal winning 19. On 22 April 1952, Gian Singh Rarewala became Chief Minister again, leading a coalition government known as the "United Front" formed by the Akali Dal and independents. His government was dismissed on 5 March 1953, and President's rule was imposed. In the subsequent mid-term election, the Congress party secured a majority, and Raghbir Singh became Chief Minister on 8 March 1954. After his death, Brish Bhan became Chief Minister on 12 January 1955 and remained in office as the last incumbent. Initially in 1948, the state was divided into eight districts and 25 sub-districts (tehsils); by 1953, the number of districts was reduced to five, with Fatehgarh Sahib and Kohistan dissolved and merged into Patiala district. Amloh and Payal tehsils of Fatehgarh Sahib were merged with Sirhind tehsil, and Dera Bassi tehsil of Kohistan was merged with Rajpura tehsil. Barnala district was abolished, with its tehsils—Phul, Dhuri, Malerkotla, and Barnala—transferred: Dhuri, Malerkotla, Barnala, and part of Phul were transferred to Sangrur, and the remainder of Phul was merged with Bhatinda. PEPSU had four Lok Sabha constituencies: Mohindergarh, Sangrur, Patiala (single-seat), and Kapurthala-Bhatinda (double-seat). The state's 1951 census recorded a population of 3,493,685, of which 19% was urban, with a population density of 133/km² and 64 towns and 5,708 villages. Its geographical coordinates are 31°27′N 77°36′E (31.45°N 77.60°E).
